registry_objects.title: Temporal Complement, revisited
registry_objects.summary: The gravitational coupling and weak coupling exhaust the depth-1 budget: kappa_tau + kappa(A;1) = (1-iota_tau) + iota_tau = 1. There is no room for a third temporal sector at depth 1, recovering the Temporal Complement Theorem from Book IV.

registry_objects.title: Relativity principle recovered
registry_objects.summary: All admissible readout functors produce the same null set C and the same speed of light c; no admissible readout functor is preferred. This recovers the relativity principle (laws of physics are the same in all inertial frames) as a corollary.

registry_objects.title: tau-Bianchi identity --- V.R01
registry_objects.summary: The tau-Einstein identity implies the tau-Bianchi identity: nabla . R^H = kappa_tau nabla . T^mat, and since boundary characters have vanishing divergence (nabla . R^H = 0), energy-momentum conservation nabla . T^mat = 0 follows as a corollary.

registry_objects.title: TOV Limit
registry_objects.summary: The coherence horizon M_n* is well-defined, finite, and positive, serving as the tau-native analogue of the Oppenheimer-Volkoff limit. Every TOV configuration with M_n > M_n* must have torus topology, by tension monotonicity and the structural threshold.

registry_objects.title: Defect support exhaustion
registry_objects.summary: Defect support exhaustion: starting from any initial configuration, defect support at depth n satisfies |supp(d_n)| <= (1 - iota_tau)^n |supp(d_0)|, and the total defect support summed over all depths is finite, bounded by |supp(d_0)|/iota_tau.

registry_objects.title: Defect entropy reaches zero
registry_objects.summary: Defect entropy reaches zero: lim_{n->inf} S_def(n) = 0 with exponentially fast convergence S_def(n) <= (1 - iota_tau)^n S_def(0). The defect entropy is driven to zero by the geometric contraction at rate (1 - iota_tau) per orbit step.

registry_objects.title: Finite irreversibility
registry_objects.summary: Finite irreversibility: every irreversible process (friction, dissipation, radioactive decay, entropy production) draws from the finite defect budget B_def <= |D_0|/iota_tau; after the coherence horizon, no further irreversible processes occur.

registry_objects.title: Vacuum source term is finite
registry_objects.summary: Vacuum source term is finite: T_vac = E_bdry/V = (1/V) integral over L of |H_partial[omega_0]|^2 d-sigma, finite and independent of any momentum cutoff; the 10^{120} discrepancy does not arise because no mode sum appears in the tau-Einstein equation.

registry_objects.title: No temporal blow-up
registry_objects.summary: No temporal blow-up: the macro tau-NS evolution on tau^3 = tau^1 x_f T^2 admits no temporal blow-up; the velocity readout is bounded at every point of the base tau^1. Follows from compactness of tau^3 and defect-horizon contractivity in the primorial (temporal) direction.

registry_objects.title: Sourceless macro flux
registry_objects.summary: Sourceless macro flux: for any closed surface Sigma in tau^3, the net B-sector flux vanishes, integral over Sigma of F_B dot d-Sigma = 0; every flux line entering a region must leave it. Gauss's law is trivially satisfied because every closed surface encloses zero net charge.

registry_objects.title: No magnetic monopoles
registry_objects.summary: No magnetic monopoles: no tau-admissible configuration on tau^3 carries a net magnetic charge; integral over Sigma of B dot d-Sigma = 0 for every closed surface Sigma. The magnetic holonomy is trivial by the same boundary structure that forces electric neutrality.

registry_objects.title: Macro color confinement
registry_objects.summary: Macro color confinement: no macroscopic configuration carries a net color charge; every hadron, nucleus, and astrophysical body is a color singlet. The C-sector contributes to the macro defect tuple only through confined composites (mesons, baryons) and cross-couplings kappa(A,C) and kappa(C,D).

registry_objects.title: Baryonic Tully--Fisher from Capacity --- V.R20
registry_objects.summary: The baryonic Tully-Fisher relation M_b = A v_infty^4 follows directly from the flat rotation curve theorem, with normalization A determined by G, c, and ell_tau (all functions of iota_tau and H_0), involving no dark matter parameter.

registry_objects.title: No Dark Matter Particle
registry_objects.summary: No particle in Category tau has dark matter properties (massive, stable, non-baryonic, not a known lepton): any massive particle must reside in one of the five sectors, and systematic elimination (D = base-only, B/C = baryonic, A = known, omega = Higgs) excludes all candidates.

registry_objects.title: No Dark Energy Field
registry_objects.summary: No field in Category tau has dark energy properties (uniform, gravitationally repulsive, not in any known sector): any such field must reside in one of the five sectors, and none produces a uniform repulsive effect. Accelerated expansion is a readout artifact.

registry_objects.title: No Fifth Force
registry_objects.summary: No fundamental interaction beyond the four forces (Gravity D, Weak A, EM B, Strong C) and Higgs mechanism (omega) exists in Category tau. The five sectors are exhaustive; a fifth force would require a sixth generator, which the Minimal Alphabet Theorem forbids.

registry_objects.title: Inflaton No-Go Corollary
registry_objects.summary: No inflaton field exists in Category tau. No new scalar sector can be added beyond the five sectors {D, A, B, C, omega} without violating Sector Exhaustion, and no new fundamental field exists beyond the five generators alpha, pi, gamma, eta, omega.

registry_objects.title: Information Preservation
registry_objects.summary: No information is lost in a tau-black hole. The boundary holonomy algebra H_partial[omega] as an inverse system preserves all data through the coherence condition. The linking class encodes the full state, and interior information is recoverable from exterior boundary characters.

registry_objects.title: No BH Evaporation
registry_objects.summary: No black hole evaporates. The ontic mass of every mature black hole is monotonically non-decreasing: M(n+1) >= M(n) for all n >= n*. The evaporation time is an artifact of chart-level interpretation. Black holes are permanent ontic objects in Category tau.

registry_objects.title: Global Finiteness
registry_objects.summary: Global Finiteness: tau^3 is globally finite, structured, and closed. (1) Finite temporal extent: t_infty = sum p_k^{-1} < infty. (2) Finite spatial extent: T^2 compact, total volume finite. (3) Finite structural vocabulary: N_eternal motifs. (4) Convergent pattern: unique absorbing state.

registry_objects.title: tau-enstrophy
registry_objects.summary: Tau-enstrophy: Omega_n = (1/2)(nu_n^macro)^2, the squared vorticity component of the macro defect tuple at primorial level n; the structural analogue of classical enstrophy, governing vorticity budget evolution across the refinement tower.

registry_objects.title: Macro charge
registry_objects.summary: Macro charge: Q^macro(d) = integral over tau^1 of Hol_B(d|_{t x T^2}) dt, the base-integrated B-sector holonomy obstruction; the macroscopic charge is the total boundary obstruction accumulated over the temporal circle.

registry_objects.title: Macro EM field
registry_objects.summary: Macro EM field: the chart-level readout of the B-sector defect components integrated over the base tau^1, F_mu-nu^macro(x) = R_mu(integral over tau^1 of D_B(t, x) dt), providing the macroscopic electromagnetic field tensor.

registry_objects.title: Macro current
registry_objects.summary: Macro current density: J^macro(x) = R_mu(q mu_B(x) v-hat_B(x)), the readout of the B-sector mobility flow, where q is the local charge, mu_B is the B-sector mobility, and v-hat_B is the unit velocity direction.

registry_objects.title: tau-plasma
registry_objects.summary: Tau-plasma: a macro defect configuration on tau^3 with nonzero B-sector defect density (n_B > 0), mobile charged carriers (mu_B > mu_crit), defining a structural plasma state through boundary obstruction density and carrier mobility conditions.

registry_objects.title: Debye number
registry_objects.summary: Debye number: N_D = n_0 lambda_D^3, the number of charge carriers in a Debye sphere. When N_D >> 1, collective effects dominate individual two-body collisions, characterizing the plasma as strongly collective.

registry_objects.title: MHD limit
registry_objects.summary: MHD limit: the magnetohydrodynamic regime of a tau-plasma where charge separation is below lambda_D, timescales exceed omega_p^{-1}, and spatial scales exceed lambda_D; the plasma is described as a single conducting fluid with frozen-flux constraint.

registry_objects.title: tau-MHD system
registry_objects.summary: Tau-MHD system: the coupled evolution of the macro tau-NS equation with Lorentz force source (J x B)/rho and the induction equation for B with Ohmic diffusion, defining the complete magnetohydrodynamic dynamics on tau^3.

registry_objects.title: Magnetic Reynolds number
registry_objects.summary: Magnetic Reynolds number: Rm = UL/eta_m = mu_0 sigma UL, where U is the characteristic velocity, L is the characteristic length, and eta_m is the magnetic diffusivity; determines whether flux is frozen in (Rm >> 1) or diffuses freely (Rm << 1).

registry_objects.title: tau-reconnection event
registry_objects.summary: Tau-reconnection event: a localized, discrete change in the topological component theta_B of the B-sector defect tuple at a specific primorial level and fiber location where Rm_local drops below the critical value; the change in topological charge is discontinuous.

registry_objects.title: MHD instability condition
registry_objects.summary: MHD instability condition: an MHD equilibrium d_0 is unstable if there exists a perturbation delta-d such that the defect functional decreases, delta[omega](d_0 + delta-d) < delta[omega](d_0); the system evolves toward the lower-energy state.

registry_objects.title: Mixed-sector mode
registry_objects.summary: Mixed-sector mode: a propagating perturbation on tau^3 involving coherent oscillation between two or more sector components of the boundary holonomy algebra; the Alfven mode is the canonical example, mixing sectors B (electromagnetic) and D (gravitational).

registry_objects.title: Alfv'en orbit
registry_objects.summary: Alfven orbit on tau^3: a trajectory gamma_A(t) in H_partial[omega] where the B-component oscillates as Hol_B = A cos(omega_A t + phi), the D-component oscillates in antiphase scaled by v_A/c, and the frequency satisfies the Alfven dispersion relation.

registry_objects.title: Macro tau-crystal
registry_objects.summary: Macro tau-crystal: a macro configuration with mu^macro = 0 (rigid), nu^macro = 0 (no vorticity), large kappa^macro (high compression rigidity), and theta^macro nonzero (long-range topological order, i.e., crystalline lattice structure).

registry_objects.title: Macro tau-glass
registry_objects.summary: Macro tau-glass: a macro configuration with mu^macro = 0 (rigid), small but nonzero nu^macro (frozen residual vorticity), large kappa^macro (high compression rigidity), and theta^macro = 0 (no long-range topological order); distinguished from crystal by absence of theta.

registry_objects.title: First-order macro transition
registry_objects.summary: First-order macro transition: a discontinuity in the macro defect tuple at base point t_0, where lim_{t->t_0^-} D^macro(t) != lim_{t->t_0^+} D^macro(t) in one or more of the four components (mu, nu, kappa, theta), representing a sharp phase boundary.

registry_objects.title: Second-order macro transition
registry_objects.summary: Second-order macro transition: at base point t_c, the macro defect tuple D^macro(t) is continuous but one or more of its derivatives dD^macro/dt are discontinuous, and a symmetry of the defect-tuple configuration is broken or restored at t_c.

registry_objects.title: Classical Validity Scale --- V.D50
registry_objects.summary: The classical validity scale ell_cl is the radius at which r |nabla C_D|/C_D >= 1, marking the transition from Newtonian inverse-square behavior to the galactic regime where capacity gradients dominate.

registry_objects.title: Angular Momentum Character --- V.D51
registry_objects.summary: The angular momentum character L_chi(n) of a D-sector boundary state chi is defined as the integral of chi wedge d theta_pi over the level-n fiber of tau^1, encoding angular momentum as a boundary holonomy property rather than a manifold symmetry.

registry_objects.title: Lensing Character --- V.D52
registry_objects.summary: The lensing character chi_lens(n) maps incoming null intertwiner directions to outgoing directions via a boundary character on S^1_in -> S^1_out, encoding gravitational lensing as a D-sector projection through the gamma-sector null structure.

registry_objects.title: Book~IV to Book~V Export Contract
registry_objects.summary: The Book IV to Book V export contract consists of ten items (arena tau^3, five sectors, sector couplings, calibration anchor, mass ratio R, defect functional, entropy splitting, tau-Einstein equation, no-shrink theorem, and G derivation), each with stated scope, forming the complete interface that Book V imports from Book IV.

registry_objects.title: Galaxy as Relational Coherence --- V.D53
registry_objects.summary: A galaxy is defined as a connected region of H_partial[omega] with D-sector capacity exceeding a coherence threshold C_min, cross-sector excitation from B and C sectors, and finite spatial extent -- a relational coherence, not a collection of gravitationally bound particles.

registry_objects.title: Cosmic Web as Capacity Skeleton --- V.D54
registry_objects.summary: The capacity skeleton is the spatial pattern of D-sector capacity C_D(x) at a given orbit depth: filaments are ridges, nodes are local maxima (galaxy clusters), voids are local minima, walls are saddle surfaces. The cosmic web is its readout.

registry_objects.title: Morphological Capacity Profile --- V.D55
registry_objects.summary: The morphological capacity profile classifies galaxies by the spatial shape of C_D(x): elliptical galaxies have slowly varying ellipsoidal profiles; spiral galaxies have disk-like profiles with non-axisymmetric perturbations producing spiral arms via density waves.

registry_objects.title: Galactic Capacity Profile --- V.D56
registry_objects.summary: For a disk galaxy with baryonic surface density Sigma_b(r), the galactic capacity profile is the solution of nabla^2 ln C_D = -(4 pi G/c^2) Sigma_b - (1/ell_tau^2) ln(C_D/C_D^infty), a nonlinear equation with tau-scale length ell_tau.

registry_objects.title: Degeneracy Pressure Character --- V.D57
registry_objects.summary: The degeneracy pressure character P_deg = ((3 pi^2)^{2/3} hbar^2 / (5 m_e)) n_e^{5/3} is the B-sector boundary character encoding the resistance of a fully occupied Fermi sea to compression, with m_e from the tau mass ratio formula.

registry_objects.title: Black Hole as Maximal Topological Defect --- V.D58
registry_objects.summary: A black hole in Category tau is a region of tau^3 where the topological defect component saturates: d_top(x) = 1 for all x in the region. The event horizon partial B is the surface where d_top transitions from <1 to 1.

registry_objects.title: Topological Channel --- V.D59
registry_objects.summary: The topological channel at x in tau^3 is the set of paths in defect space that increase d_top(x). It is closed when all such paths require energy input, and open when at least one path is energetically favorable.

registry_objects.title: Channel Reversal --- V.D60
registry_objects.summary: A channel reversal occurs when the topological channel that was favorable in one direction (increasing d_top) becomes unfavorable, and the reverse direction becomes favorable. At the bounce, C-sector nuclear pressure exceeds D-sector compression, redirecting collapse energy outward.

registry_objects.title: r-Process as Rapid Charge Loading --- V.D61
registry_objects.summary: The r-process is the rapid sequential addition of C-sector (Strong) charge units (neutrons) to a seed nucleus: (Z,A) + n -> (Z, A+1) + gamma, repeated ~10-100 times faster than beta-decay (A-sector charge conversion), populating heavy element configurations.

registry_objects.title: Accretion Funnel (tau-geodesic)
registry_objects.summary: The accretion funnel of a coherent instance with toroidal boundary L is the region of tau^3 where infalling geodesics converge toward the equatorial plane of T^2, with angular momentum transport through the lemniscate crossing controlled by kappa(omega) = iota_tau^3/(1+iota_tau).

registry_objects.title: OnticParticle --- IV.D22
registry_objects.summary: An ontic particle is a defect bundle p in Def(T^2) satisfying persistence (rho-invariance), unique sector decomposition p = p_B + p_C + p_omega into EM, Strong, and Higgs components, and a mass condition; it is a topologically stable boundary holonomy configuration on the fiber, not a point excitation of a quantum field.

registry_objects.title: Jet Axis (Topological Channel)
registry_objects.summary: The jet axis of a coherent instance is the one-dimensional subspace of tau^3 aligned with the base generator alpha, located within the torus hole (r < r_hole = R(1-iota_tau)), with two components (north/south poles) corresponding to bipolar jet lobes.

registry_objects.title: Synchrotron Readout
registry_objects.summary: The synchrotron readout of an accretion funnel is the EM spectral power P_sync(nu) = (sqrt(3) e^3 B / (m_e c^2)) F(nu/nu_c) emitted by charged defect bundles spiraling in the gamma-sector field, with the sqrt(3) factor being the lemniscate spectral distance |1-omega|.

registry_objects.title: AGN Lifecycle Phase
registry_objects.summary: The AGN lifecycle phase is the pair (M_dot/M_dot_Edd, theta_obs): the normalized accretion rate encodes the evolutionary state (quasar -> Seyfert -> LINER -> quiescent) and the observation angle determines the apparent type (Type 1 vs Type 2).

registry_objects.title: Binary Coherent-Instance System
registry_objects.summary: A binary coherent-instance system is a pair (I_1, I_2) of coherent instances on tau^3 sharing the same base tau^1 progression (same temporal depth), with mutual boundary holonomy H_12 governing their gravitational interaction.

registry_objects.title: GW Boundary-Character Wave
registry_objects.summary: A gravitational-wave boundary-character wave is a time-dependent perturbation delta H^D(t) of the D-sector boundary holonomy algebra, propagating at speed c. The two polarizations (plus and cross) correspond to the two traceless symmetric deformation modes of the fiber T^2.

registry_objects.title: Ringdown Readout
registry_objects.summary: The ringdown readout of a merged coherent instance is the quasi-normal mode decomposition h(t) = sum A_n exp(-t/tau_n) cos(2 pi f_n t + phi_n), where each mode has a frequency f_n and damping time tau_n determined by the final mass M_f.

registry_objects.title: Standard Siren (tau)
registry_objects.summary: A standard siren is a binary merger whose GW signal provides a direct luminosity distance measurement d_L from the chirp mass and observed strain, requiring no empirical calibration step: the intrinsic amplitude is determined by M_c alone.

registry_objects.title: Toroidal Shadow (T^2 Readout)
registry_objects.summary: The toroidal shadow of a coherent instance with T^2 topology, major radius R, minor radius r = iota_tau R, viewed at inclination iota, is the closed curve on the observer's sky defined by critical impact parameters of null geodesics around the photon torus.

registry_objects.title: Photon Ring Winding Number
registry_objects.summary: The photon ring winding number n is the number of half-orbits a photon completes around the photon torus before escaping to the observer. Subrings indexed by n are nested, with the n-th subring lying inside the (n-1)-th subring.

registry_objects.title: Polarization Handedness Signature
registry_objects.summary: The polarization handedness signature is the EVPA winding number w_EVPA = (1/2pi) oint dchi around the shadow boundary, encoding the magnetic field geometry. For toroidal topology with toroidal B-field, w_EVPA = 2; for radial B-field (S^2), w_EVPA = 1.

registry_objects.title: Defect Tuple --- IV.D20
registry_objects.summary: The defect tuple D(phi) = (d_mob, d_vor, d_com, d_top) of a configuration phi in H_partial[omega] encodes the deviation from vacuum as four components: mobility, vorticity, compression, and topological charge, forming the key export from Book IV's many-body physics.

registry_objects.title: Boundary-Mass Offset (tau)
registry_objects.summary: The boundary-mass offset Delta x = |x_lensing - x_gas| is the spatial separation between the baryonic mass centroid (X-ray gas) and the total gravitational mass centroid (weak lensing), arising because boundary holonomy mass M_partial concentrates at coherent instances.

registry_objects.title: Handle-Scale Event
registry_objects.summary: A handle-scale event is a dynamical process involving rearrangement of boundary holonomy at spatial scales comparable to the major radius R ~ R_S/iota_tau = 2GM/(iota_tau c^2) of the tau^3 fibration.

registry_objects.title: Wilson Skeleton (Cosmic Web)
registry_objects.summary: The Wilson skeleton W(L) at readout scale L is the network of holonomy loops on the base tau^1 with circumference <= L. Its image gives the cosmic web structure: nodes = clusters, edges = filaments, enclosed regions = voids.

registry_objects.title: Topological Lensing Signature
registry_objects.summary: The topological lensing signature is the additional light deflection Delta theta_top = oint kappa_tau Omega_D ds accumulated along a light ray's path through the Wilson skeleton, beyond standard gravitational lensing, with kappa_tau = 1 - iota_tau.

registry_objects.title: Sector Budget
registry_objects.summary: The sector budget B(n) = {kappa(X; n) | X in {A,B,C,D,omega}} partitions the total coupling into sector contributions at orbit depth n, subject to a normalization constraint analogous to a probability distribution (total sums to 1, all non-negative).

registry_objects.title: Sector Exhaustion Decomposition
registry_objects.summary: The sector exhaustion decomposition H_partial[omega] = H_A + H_B + H_C + H_D + H_omega is the direct-sum decomposition of the boundary holonomy algebra into its four primitive sector components plus the crossing component, with mutually orthogonal sectors.

registry_objects.title: Dark Sector Hypothesis
registry_objects.summary: The dark sector hypothesis posits a nonzero tau-algebra component H_dark that is EM-invisible (no B-sector coupling), gravitationally active (D-sector coupling), and not contained in any of the five sectors {H_A, H_B, H_C, H_D, H_omega}.

registry_objects.title: Readout Artifact
registry_objects.summary: A readout artifact is a quantity that appears nonzero in the orthodox readout (tau-native structure projected onto a classical manifold) but corresponds to no independent substance or field in Category tau. Dark energy (Omega_Lambda ~ 0.68) is the principal readout artifact.

registry_objects.title: Orbit-Depth-Dependent Readout
registry_objects.summary: An orbit-depth-dependent readout is a physical quantity whose measured value depends on the orbit depth n at which measurement is performed, defined as the restriction of an observable O on H_partial[omega] to the level-n truncation of the refinement tower.

registry_objects.title: Depth-Projected Hubble Parameter
registry_objects.summary: The depth-projected Hubble parameter H(n) = H_infty (1 + delta H / iota_tau^n) approaches H_infty at large n (early universe) and takes larger values at small n (late universe), with the depth correction delta H driven by the defect structure of the progression operator.

registry_objects.title: Base Circle tau^1 (Macroscopic)
registry_objects.summary: The base circle tau^1 is the one-dimensional compact profinite space generated by the two base generators alpha (Gravity/D-sector) and pi (Weak/A-sector), equipped with the alpha-orbit O_alpha = {alpha_n : n >= 1} and the profinite topology inherited from the refinement tower R = (alpha_n, rho_n).

registry_objects.title: Category Error (LCDM)
registry_objects.summary: Lambda-CDM commits three category errors: identifying boundary holonomy mass as a new matter particle (dark matter as substance), the progression rate as a cosmological constant (dark energy as field), and the readout projection as a fundamental spacetime manifold.

registry_objects.title: Readout Projection Table
registry_objects.summary: The readout projection table translates each Lambda-CDM parameter into its tau-native counterpart, preserving numerical values while changing ontological interpretation: same numbers, different story.

registry_objects.title: Temporal Opening
registry_objects.summary: The temporal opening is the structural transition from the pre-temporal kernel specification to the first refinement level alpha_1 = alpha. It is unique (exactly one first level), irreversible (no pre-alpha_1 state), and maximal in boundary-character energy density.

registry_objects.title: Pre-Hadronic Regime
registry_objects.summary: The pre-hadronic regime R_pre is the interval of alpha-ticks from the temporal opening alpha_1 to the neutron threshold L_N, i.e., {alpha_n : 1 <= n < n_N}. Before n_N, no stable composite nucleons exist as persistent defect bundles on T^2.

registry_objects.title: Regime Boundary Character
registry_objects.summary: A regime boundary character chi_n at refinement depth n is the restriction chi_n = ev_n composed with chi in H_partial[omega]_n, where ev_n evaluates the full boundary character at depth n. It captures the spectral content available at a given refinement level.

registry_objects.title: Regime Invariance
registry_objects.summary: A dynamical equation on tau^1 is regime-invariant if its structural form -- the algebraic identity relating curvature, coupling, and source -- is independent of the refinement depth n. The tau-Einstein equation's structure does not change across cosmological epochs.

registry_objects.title: Inflationary Regime
registry_objects.summary: The inflationary regime is the sub-interval of the pre-hadronic regime during which the chart-level readout yields approximately exponential expansion: a(alpha_{n+1})/a(alpha_n) > e^delta. It begins at the temporal opening and ends when boundary characters decrease below the threshold.

registry_objects.title: e-Fold Readout
registry_objects.summary: The e-fold readout N_e is the total number of e-folds accumulated during the inflationary regime: N_e = sum over n in R_inf of ln(a(alpha_{n+1})/a(alpha_n)). The primorial structure naturally produces N_e >> 60, far exceeding the orthodox minimum requirement.

registry_objects.title: Threshold (Regime Boundary)
registry_objects.summary: A threshold at refinement depth n_* is a critical depth where a qualitative change occurs in the regime boundary character chi_n: a sector coupling or cross-coupling function f_X(chi_n) crosses a critical value f_X^crit, producing a phase transition in the physical readout.

registry_objects.title: Canonical Thresholds
registry_objects.summary: The canonical threshold ladder is the ordered sequence of six regime transitions: L_EW (electroweak) -> L_B (baryogenesis) -> L_N (neutron) -> L_nuc (nucleosynthesis) -> L_H (hydrogen recombination) -> L_gamma (photon decoupling, z ~ 1100).

registry_objects.title: Alpha-Tick
registry_objects.summary: An alpha-tick Delta_n := (alpha_n -> alpha_{n+1}) is the passage from one refinement tower level to the next under rho; it is the elementary temporal unit of Category tau -- the structural quantum of temporal progression, not a Planck time derived from dimensional analysis.

registry_objects.title: Neutron Threshold L_N
registry_objects.summary: The neutron threshold L_N is the refinement depth n_N at which the Strong-sector (eta) character drops below the confinement critical value kappa(C; 3) = iota_tau^3/(1 - iota_tau), and stable composite nucleons appear as persistent defect bundles on T^2.

registry_objects.title: Nucleosynthetic Window
registry_objects.summary: The nucleosynthetic window W_nuc is the interval of refinement depths [n_nuc^open, n_nuc^close] during which light nuclei can be synthesized: deuterium survives above the open threshold, and the window closes when the expansion rate exceeds the nuclear reaction rate.

registry_objects.title: Threshold Ladder
registry_objects.summary: The threshold ladder is the complete ordered sequence of canonical thresholds together with the regime boundary characters at each threshold and the physical readout that changes at each crossing, providing a unified description of all cosmological phase transitions.

registry_objects.title: Gravitational Tension
registry_objects.summary: Gravitational tension at a region U in tau^3 is G(U) = kappa(D;1) * ||T[chi]|_U||, where kappa(D;1) = 1 - iota_tau is the gravitational self-coupling and ||.|| is the boundary norm on H_partial[omega]. It measures the gravitational field strength generated by matter in U.

registry_objects.title: Spherical Capacity
registry_objects.summary: The spherical capacity C_sph(n) of the fiber T^2 at base point alpha_n is the supremum of gravitational tension G(U) over all contractible subsets U of T^2. It is the maximum gravitational tension the fiber can sustain while remaining topologically contractible.

registry_objects.title: Linking Class
registry_objects.summary: A linking class in tau^3 is a non-contractible cycle ell in H_1(T^2; Z) = Z + Z that links the two generators of pi_1(T^2). It is non-trivial if both components ell = (a, b) satisfy ab != 0, wrapping around both cycles of the torus fiber.

registry_objects.title: Black Hole (Topological Event)
registry_objects.summary: A black hole in Category tau is the emergence of a non-trivial linking class ell in H_1(T^2; Z) at a base point alpha_{n_*} where the gravitational tension exceeds the spherical capacity: G(U_{n_*}) > C_sph(n_*). The BH is a topological event, not a metric singularity.

registry_objects.title: Canonical BH Neighborhood
registry_objects.summary: The canonical BH neighborhood N_BH is the open subset of tau^3 consisting of all points (alpha_n, x) with n >= n_* (birth depth) and gravitational tension G(alpha_n, x) > C_sph. It is the spacetime region occupied by the black hole from birth onward.

registry_objects.title: BH Bipolarity
registry_objects.summary: A black hole with linking class ell = (a,b) is bipolar if its boundary character chi_BH restricted to the linking boundary has nonzero components on both lobes: chi_BH^+ != 0 and chi_BH^- != 0. Bipolarity reflects the chi_+/chi_- spectral decomposition of the lemniscate.

registry_objects.title: Polarity Imbalance
registry_objects.summary: The polarity imbalance I_BH = (||chi_BH^+|| - ||chi_BH^-||)/(||chi_BH^+|| + ||chi_BH^-||) in (-1,1) measures asymmetry between the two lemniscate lobes. I = 0 is perfect bipolarity; the necessary bipolarity theorem prevents I from reaching the unipolar limits +/-1.

registry_objects.title: Proper Time (Arc Length)
registry_objects.summary: Proper time t(n) := sum_{k=1}^{n-1} ell(Delta_k) is the accumulated arc length along the alpha-orbit from alpha_1 to alpha_n, where ell(Delta_k) = p_k^{-1} is the geodesic distance between consecutive levels. The series converges absolutely to a finite limit t_infinity.

registry_objects.title: Blueprint

registry_objects.summary: The BAO standard ruler is the comoving sound horizon at the recombination orbit depth n_rec: r_s(n_rec) = R_d[integral c_s(n) dell/dn dn], where c_s(n) is the baryon-photon fluid sound speed. The inputs -- baryon-to-photon ratio, photon energy density, kappa(D;1) = 1 - iota_tau -- are all derived from iota_tau.

registry_objects.title: Cumulative Topology Change
registry_objects.summary: N_BH(n) = count of independent non-contractible BH linking classes in H_1(T^2_n; Z) at refinement depth n. Non-decreasing by No-Shrink Theorem; mergers reduce count via linking-class composition but BHs cannot disappear.

registry_objects.title: Wilson-Loop Superstructure
registry_objects.summary: Graph S(n) whose vertices are BH excision neighborhoods and edges are Wilson loops connecting them. Cosmic web of filaments, walls, and voids is the chart-level readout of these linking relations.

registry_objects.title: omega-Germ Normalizer Norm_omega
registry_objects.summary: For an omega-germ sequence g = (g_n), the omega-germ normalizer is Norm_omega(g)_n := NF_n(g_n), applying the canonical normal form function at each stage n of the boundary character at the crossing point.

registry_objects.title: Stability Index of omega-Germ
registry_objects.summary: For an omega-germ g, the stability index n_*(g) is the minimal stage at which Norm_omega(g) stabilizes under refinement. Beyond n_*(g), the germ has reached its final normal form.

registry_objects.title: Admissible Endomorphism Monoid HolEnd^adm_tau
registry_objects.summary: Sub-monoid of End(Germ_omega) preserving holonomy grading and sigma-involution. H_partial[omega] is isomorphic to HolEnd^adm_tau as graded monoids at E1. Admissibility is the tau-native analogue of gauge fixing.

registry_objects.title: Readout curvature
registry_objects.summary: The readout curvature kappa_R(n) := d^2 R_d / dn^2 is the second derivative of the distance readout functor with respect to orbit depth. When kappa_R(n) != 0, equal orbit-depth intervals map to unequal SI-length intervals. Scope: conjectural (explicit form deferred to Part V).

registry_objects.title: Recombination orbit depth
registry_objects.summary: The recombination orbit depth n_rec is the orbit depth on tau^1 at which the omega-sector binding energy (Higgs/mass mechanism) exceeds the gamma-sector photon energy for hydrogen-like boundary characters. At n_rec photons decouple and become free-streaming null intertwiners; z_rec ~ 1100 is reproduced from iota_tau-derived sector couplings.

registry_objects.title: CMB constraint surface
registry_objects.summary: The CMB constraint surface Sigma_CMB = H_partial[omega]|_{n=n_rec} is the state of the boundary holonomy algebra at the recombination orbit depth, encoding the mean temperature (gamma-sector energy scale), the anisotropy spectrum (angular character distribution), and the polarization pattern.

registry_objects.title: Neutrino decoupling orbit depth
registry_objects.summary: The neutrino decoupling orbit depth n_nu is the orbit depth at which the pi-sector (weak force) interaction rate Gamma_pi(n_nu) drops below the base progression rate on tau^1. Since n_nu < n_rec, the cosmic neutrino background encodes H_partial[omega] at an earlier, higher-energy orbit depth.

registry_objects.title: CnuB echo surface
registry_objects.summary: The CnuB echo surface Sigma_{CnuB} = H_partial[omega]|_{n=n_nu} is the boundary holonomy algebra at the neutrino decoupling depth, encoding the neutrino energy spectrum (Fermi-Dirac at T_nu), the number of neutrino species (3 from A-sector structure), and their mass spectrum.

registry_objects.title: Cosmic Stack API
registry_objects.summary: The Cosmic Stack API is the formal interface between Part I and Parts II-VIII: fixed inputs include arc-length time, three epochs, initial conditions, photon ontology, redshift-depth relation, readout functor, two constraint surfaces, and the Cosmic Stack; each subsequent Part has required outputs and scope targets.

registry_objects.title: Clopen frame
registry_objects.summary: A clopen frame at depth n is a pair (U_k^(n), e_k^(n)) where U_k^(n) = [alpha_k, alpha_{k+1}] is the k-th clopen arc of tau^1 and e_k^(n) = (e_gamma, e_eta, e_omega) is a coherence basis for the fiber T^2 over that arc.

registry_objects.title: Frame holonomy on tau^1
registry_objects.summary: The frame holonomy at depth n is the composition Hol_n = Phi_{p_n-1,0}^(n) circ ... circ Phi_{0,1}^(n) of all frame adjacency maps around the base circle tau^1, yielding an element of Aut(T^2_{alpha_0}).

registry_objects.title: Holonomy gap element
registry_objects.summary: The local gap element Delta_k^(n) = Phi_{k,k+1}^(n) - Id_{T^2} in End(T^2_{alpha_{k+1}}) measures the per-arc deviation from flatness. The total gap element at depth n sums these local contributions over all p_n arcs.

registry_objects.title: Torus vacuum --- V.D01
registry_objects.summary: The torus vacuum is the stabilized torus configuration of tau^3 beyond the maturity horizon n*, characterized by the shape ratio r/R = iota_tau = 2/(pi+e). The shape ratio is fixed by refinement coherence; only the overall scale R remains free.

registry_objects.title: Gravitational constant --- V.D02
registry_objects.summary: The gravitational constant G_tau = (c^3/hbar) iota_tau^2 is the coherence conversion invariant translating between the tau-native D-sector coupling kappa(D;1) = 1 - iota_tau and the experimentally measured G. In Planck units, G_tau = iota_tau^2.

registry_objects.title: Gravitational coupling kappa_tau
registry_objects.summary: The gravitational coupling kappa_tau = kappa(D;1) = 1 - iota_tau approximately equals 0.658696. This is the unique depth-1 coupling in the D-sector and serves as the coefficient in the tau-Einstein equation.

registry_objects.title: Null intertwiner
registry_objects.summary: A null intertwiner is an element phi in H_partial[omega] whose temporal component (D-sector projection) and spatial component (fiber sector projection) satisfy ||pr_D(phi)||^2 = ||pr_fiber(phi)||^2 under the boundary character pairing.

registry_objects.title: Local tau^3 chart
registry_objects.summary: A local tau^3 chart is a readout functor R_p: H_partial[omega] -> O_p centered at a base point p in tau^1, where O_p is a Minkowski vector space of signature (1,3). The chart is valid in a neighborhood U_p of the base point.

registry_objects.title: Curvature character --- V.D04
registry_objects.summary: The curvature character R^H is the D-sector boundary projection of the frame holonomy gap: R^H_n(x) = eta_n(T^GR_n(x)) in H_partial^(D), where T^GR_n(x) is the minimal GR budget (smallest alpha-index) at base point x and depth n.

registry_objects.title: Matter character --- V.D03
registry_objects.summary: The matter character T^mat is the direct sum of the EM, weak, and strong sector boundary projections: T^mat_n(x) = eta_n(T^EM_n(x) + T^wk_n(x) + T^s_n(x)). Gravity appears on the curvature side, not the matter side; the omega-sector is encoded through crossing-point coupling.

registry_objects.title: tau-Einstein equation --- V.D06
registry_objects.summary: The tau-Einstein equation is the boundary-character identity R^H(x) = kappa_tau * T^mat(x) in H_partial[omega], where R^H is the curvature character, kappa_tau = 1-iota_tau is the gravitational coupling, and T^mat is the matter character. It is algebraic, not a PDE.

registry_objects.title: Linearized tau-Einstein equation
registry_objects.summary: The linearized tau-Einstein equation is the first-order expansion: R^H_lin(x) = kappa_tau * T^mat_lin(x) + O(epsilon^2), where epsilon measures the weak-field regime (frame holonomy deviating only slightly from the identity).

registry_objects.title: Gravitational wave in tau-framework
registry_objects.summary: A gravitational wave in the tau-framework is a propagating perturbation delta Delta_k^(n) of the holonomy gap elements satisfying the linearized tau-Einstein equation with T^mat_lin = 0 (vacuum perturbation).

registry_objects.title: Cocycle defect
registry_objects.summary: The cocycle defect Delta(chi) = G_omega(chi) - kappa_tau * T^mat_omega(chi) in H_partial[omega] measures how far a candidate boundary character chi departs from satisfying the tau-Einstein identity. A character is Einstein-admissible iff Delta(chi) = 0.

registry_objects.title: tau-NF Einstein iteration
registry_objects.summary: The tau-NF Einstein iteration is the sequence {chi_n} in H_partial[omega] starting from the linearized solution chi_{n_0}, with update chi_{n+1} = NF_omega(chi_n - lambda_n * Delta(chi_n)). The iteration terminates at depth n* when Delta(chi_{n*}) = 0 exactly.

registry_objects.title: Truncation-coherent descent
registry_objects.summary: The step size lambda_n in the NF Einstein iteration is truncation-coherent if it satisfies compatibility (truncation pi_n(chi_{n+1}) = chi_n) and monotonicity (the cocycle defect norm decreases at each step).

registry_objects.title: Density-saturated character
registry_objects.summary: A boundary character chi is density-saturated at depth n* if ||T^mat_omega(chi)||_{n*} = C_{n*} / kappa_tau, where C_{n*} is the profinite bound from the density cap theorem. The depth n* is the saturation depth.

registry_objects.title: Null intertwiner
registry_objects.summary: The null intertwiner at orbit depth n is the map N_n: H_partial^base[alpha,pi]|_n -> H_partial^fiber[gamma,eta,omega]|_n that sends the base component of a boundary character to the fiber component via the cross-coupling structure at the crossing point of L.

registry_objects.title: Present surface
registry_objects.summary: The present surface at orbit depth n is Sigma_n = Im(N_n) in H_partial^fiber[gamma,eta,omega]|_n, the maximal set of fiber configurations that can exchange information with the base at depth n.

registry_objects.title: tau-Horizon
registry_objects.summary: A tau-horizon is an orbit depth n_H at which the present surface contracts: Sigma_{n_H} is strictly contained in Sigma_{n_H-1}. The boundary character at the horizon depth has a density-saturated D-sector component.

registry_objects.title: Torus vacuum --- V.D01
registry_objects.summary: The torus vacuum (ch16 restatement of V.D01) is the stabilized boundary character of a mature gravitational state in H_partial[omega], characterized by the minor radius index r_n(x) (fiber dimension) and the major radius index R_n(x) (base dimension).

registry_objects.title: Gravitational constant --- V.D02
registry_objects.summary: The tau-gravitational constant G_tau (ch16 restatement) is defined as G_tau = R_n(x_min)/(2 M_n(x_min)), the coherence conversion invariant relating the mass index to the major radius index, where x_min is the minimal mature state. The factor 2 reflects the bi-lobed lemniscate.

registry_objects.title: Geometric relaxation
registry_objects.summary: Geometric relaxation is the process by which the torus vacuum adjusts its shape ratio toward r/R = iota_tau via the NF iteration. The geometric relaxation timescale t_geom ~ R_S / (c * (1-iota_tau)) is set by the gravitational sector coupling.

registry_objects.title: Topological relaxation
registry_objects.summary: Topological relaxation is the process by which the torus vacuum settles the relative orientation of its two non-contractible cycles (gamma-cycle and eta-cycle) through (gamma, eta)-sector coupling. The topological timescale is longer than the geometric timescale.

registry_objects.title: BH evolution modes --- V.D09
registry_objects.summary: The three tau-admissible BH evolution modes are: (1) Ringdown -- internal normalization without changing M; (2) Transport -- boundary-induced holomorphic transport; (3) Accretion -- mass increase through boundary absorption. Mass is preserved or increased, never decreased.

registry_objects.title: Spherical carrier predicate
registry_objects.summary: A boundary character chi satisfies the spherical carrier predicate Sph(chi) if its fiber component is invariant under gamma <-> eta exchange (fiber isotropy, tau-native S^2 isotropy) and its base component is smooth (convergent profinite expansion at all depths).

registry_objects.title: Equilibrium carrier
registry_objects.summary: An equilibrium carrier is a boundary character chi satisfying the spherical carrier predicate Sph(chi), the stationarity condition rho(chi|_{tau^1}) = chi|_{tau^1} (no evolution along the alpha-orbit), and the tau-Einstein identity.

registry_objects.title: GR tension functional
registry_objects.summary: The GR tension functional T[chi] = sum_{n >= n_0} iota_tau^n ||G_omega(chi)|_n - G_omega(chi_flat)|_n||_n^2 measures the total deviation of a configuration from the flat torus vacuum, weighted by iota_tau^n at each orbit depth.

registry_objects.title: Tension profile
registry_objects.summary: The tension profile t(n) = ||G_omega(chi)|_n - G_omega(chi_flat)|_n||_n^2 for n >= n_0 describes the orbit-depth-resolved gravitational cost of an equilibrium carrier, showing how curvature character deviates from the flat vacuum at each depth.

registry_objects.title: Canonical star builder
registry_objects.summary: The canonical star builder Star_n(k): N_{>0} x {D,A,B,C,omega} -> H_partial[omega] takes baryon count n and dominant sector index k as input and produces the unique equilibrium carrier representing the stellar configuration via the NF Einstein iteration.

registry_objects.title: Neutron node
registry_objects.summary: A neutron node at orbit depth n is a local minimum of the strong-sector confinement functional kappa(C;3) = iota_tau^3/(1-iota_tau) applied to the fiber component of the equilibrium carrier Star_n(C). Each neutron occupies a specific orbit depth and fiber address.

registry_objects.title: Node density and confinement tension
registry_objects.summary: The node density nu(n) counts occupied neutron nodes at orbit depth n. The confinement tension T_C(n) measures the strong-sector contribution to the GR tension functional from the carrier's strong-sector component chi_C|_n at that depth.

registry_objects.title: EW-stable node
registry_objects.summary: A neutron node Node(n,j) is EW-stable if every weak-sector perturbation delta_A * chi_A at that node increases the total GR tension functional: T[chi + delta_A * chi_A] > T[chi] for all delta_A != 0. Converting a neutron to a proton costs energy.

registry_objects.title: Chandrasekhar threshold
registry_objects.summary: The Chandrasekhar threshold n_Ch is the critical baryon count at which the star builder transitions from Star_n(A) (weak-sector support, white dwarf) to Star_n(C) (strong-sector support, neutron star) or Star_n(D) (gravitational self-support, black hole).

registry_objects.title: GR Tension Functional
registry_objects.summary: The GR tension functional for a TOV star configuration x with mass M and ball carrier B^3 is T_n(x) = sup_{y in partial B^3} ||G_n(y)|| / (||T^mat_n(y)|| + epsilon_n), measuring the curvature-to-matter ratio at the carrier boundary.

registry_objects.title: Coherence Horizon
registry_objects.summary: The coherence horizon M_n*(x) is the maximal mass index for which the GR tension functional remains bounded by the structural threshold Lambda_tau: M_n* = sup{M | T_n(x_M) <= Lambda_tau}. Beyond it, ball topology cannot accommodate a refinement-coherent solution.

registry_objects.title: Topology Crossing Event
registry_objects.summary: A topology crossing event at orbit depth n is a transition x_n^(ball) -> x_{n+1}^(torus) from a ball-topology configuration at the structural threshold to a torus-topology configuration that is a valid torus vacuum. The topology change is discontinuous.

registry_objects.title: Calibration Constant Xi_tau
registry_objects.summary: The tau-relative calibration constant Xi_tau = lim_{n->omega} M_n* / m_n^(tau) is the omega-germ ratio of the coherence horizon to the neutron mass index. Both are tau-native quantities; no SI units enter its definition.

registry_objects.title: Calibration Triangle
registry_objects.summary: The calibration triangle Delta_tau = (N, T, B) = (m_n^(tau), M_n*, M_n^(BH,min)) consists of three tau-native mass indices (neutron, TOV threshold, minimal BH) with three edge ratios Xi_tau^(NT), Xi_tau^(TB), Xi_tau^(NB) satisfying Xi_tau^(NB) = Xi_tau^(NT) * Xi_tau^(TB).

registry_objects.title: Ring Homomorphism Phi_p,n
registry_objects.summary: The ring homomorphism Phi_{p,n}: R_partial^(micro) -> R_partial^(meso) is the boundary-ring map Lift_D circ Scale_{Xi_tau^(NT)} circ Embed_{A->D}, connecting the proton-neutron mass split (micro vertex) to the TOV scale (meso vertex) through sector-coupling algebra.

registry_objects.title: Gravitational Closing Identity --- V.D11
registry_objects.summary: The gravitational closing identity is alpha_G = alpha^18 * (chi kappa_n / 2), where alpha_G = G m_n^2 / (hbar c) is the gravitational fine-structure constant, alpha is the EM fine-structure constant, kappa_n is the co-rotor coupling, and chi is the chirality factor.

registry_objects.title: Corrected Co-Rotor Coupling --- V.D10
registry_objects.summary: The corrected co-rotor coupling is kappa_n = kappa_n^(tree) * (1 - c_1 * alpha) with c_1 = 3/pi approximately 0.95493, arising from three lemniscate sectors each contributing 1/pi holonomy units. The identification c_1 = 3/pi is conjectural (0.04% numerical match).

registry_objects.title: Thermodynamic equilibrium---categorical
registry_objects.summary: Categorical thermodynamic equilibrium: a configuration omega_eq on tau^3 with vanishing defect entropy S_def[omega_eq] = 0, meaning all holomorphic continuations are structurally trivial -- no defect bundles, no non-holomorphic insertions, no physically resolvable disorder.

registry_objects.title: Coherence horizon
registry_objects.summary: Coherence horizon: the orbit depth n_coh = min{n in N : S_def(n) = 0} at which defect entropy first reaches zero; for n >= n_coh the configuration is in categorical equilibrium. Existence and finiteness guaranteed by the Global Defect Exhaustion Theorem.

registry_objects.title: Defect partition of paths
registry_objects.summary: Defect partition of paths: at orbit depth n, CR-compatible paths of length <= r from node n are classified as defect-traversing (passing through at least one defect site where |dbar_b f| > 0) or defect-free (avoiding all defect sites in D_n).

registry_objects.title: Defect entropy
registry_objects.summary: Defect entropy at orbit depth n: S_def(n) = lim_{r->inf} (1/r) ln(1 + P_def(n,r)), measuring the exponential growth rate of defect-traversing paths; the +1 inside the logarithm ensures S_def = 0 when the defect path count vanishes (vacuum).

registry_objects.title: Refinement entropy
registry_objects.summary: Refinement entropy at orbit depth n: S_ref(n) = lim_{r->inf} (1/r) ln P_free(n,r), counting the exponential growth rate of defect-free holomorphic paths; these paths exist even in the vacuum because the lattice itself provides defect-free continuations.

registry_objects.title: Global defect budget
registry_objects.summary: Global defect budget: B_def = sum_{n=0}^{inf} |D_n|, the total defect support summed over all orbit depths, measuring the universe's total capacity for irreversible processes.

registry_objects.title: Coherence horizon---refined
registry_objects.summary: Coherence horizon (refined): n_coh = min{n in N : |D_n| = 0}, the smallest orbit depth at which the defect set is empty. By the Global Defect Exhaustion Theorem, this minimum exists and is finite; for p = 2 the bound gives n_coh <= 398.

registry_objects.title: Defect half-life
registry_objects.summary: Defect half-life: n_{1/2} = ln 2 / (-ln(1 - iota_tau)) approx 1.66 orbit steps, the number of orbit steps for the defect count to halve. Controlled by the gravitational self-coupling; every approximately two orbit steps, half of remaining defects are absorbed.

registry_objects.title: EM energy transport
registry_objects.summary: EM energy transport: a change in the CR-tension distribution on tau^3 mediated by the B-sector of H_partial[omega], with energy Delta E_transport = integral over tau^3 of the pairing between the B-sector boundary holonomy variation and dbar_b f.

registry_objects.title: Geometric relaxation
registry_objects.summary: Geometric relaxation: the process by which a defect bundle loses CR-tension through spatial redistribution on the fiber T^2, driven by the fiber gradient of |dbar_b f|^2 weighted by the B-sector self-coupling kappa(B;2).

registry_objects.title: Topological relaxation
registry_objects.summary: Topological relaxation: the process by which a defect bundle is absorbed by the lemniscate boundary L = S^1 v S^1 through a change in topological sector, with energy release given by the variation of the boundary holonomy integral over L.

registry_objects.title: The tau-vacuum
registry_objects.summary: The tau-vacuum: the ground configuration omega_0 in H_partial[omega] satisfying dbar_b omega_0 = 0 everywhere (holomorphic throughout), S_def[omega_0] = 0 (zero defect entropy), and E[omega_0] = E_bdry (energy equals the boundary energy).

registry_objects.title: Capacity surplus
registry_objects.summary: Capacity surplus: C_surplus(n) = C_total - |D_n|, the difference between the total absorption capacity of the lemniscate L and the current defect count; unused boundary capacity manifests as negative pressure in the effective equation of state.

registry_objects.title: Macro defect-transport equation
registry_objects.summary: Macro defect-transport equation: D^macro_{n+1} = pr_base(Phi_{n,n+1}(d_n)), the base-projected evolution of the 4-component defect tuple (mu, nu, kappa, theta), where the fiber contributions from B, C, omega sectors are averaged and enter only through cross-couplings.

registry_objects.title: Macro tau-Navier--Stokes flow
registry_objects.summary: Macro tau-Navier-Stokes flow: a sequence of tau-admissible configurations satisfying base-sector (D and A) dominance and macro viscous decay B^macro_{n+1} - B^macro_n proportional to the viscosity correction, defining the macroscopic fluid evolution on tau^3.

registry_objects.title: Macro tau-Reynolds number
registry_objects.summary: Macro tau-Reynolds number: Re_tau^macro = mu_n^macro / eta_tau^macro, the ratio of macro mobility to macro viscosity; determines whether the flow is laminar (Re << 1) or turbulent (Re >> 1).

registry_objects.title: tau-turbulent flow
registry_objects.summary: Tau-turbulent flow: a macro tau-NS flow with Re_tau^macro >> 1, non-monotonic defect budget B_n^macro across primorial levels n_inj <= n <= n_diss, and structured variation where budget decrease at each level is balanced by injection from the source. Turbulence is deterministic but structurally complex.

registry_objects.title: Surface Matter Bound
registry_objects.summary: For any TOV configuration with mass M and carrier radius R, the surface matter character satisfies sup ||T^mat_n(y)|| <= C_pack * R_n^2(x), where C_pack is the universal maximal packing constant for persistent defect bundles on the ball carrier surface.

registry_objects.title: Geometric contraction of defect support
registry_objects.summary: Geometric contraction lemma for defect support: if a_{n+1} <= (1 - iota_tau) a_n, then a_n <= (1 - iota_tau)^n a_0, the series sum_{n>=0} a_n <= a_0/iota_tau is finite, and a_n -> 0. The contraction factor is the gravitational coupling.

registry_objects.title: Integer threshold
registry_objects.summary: Integer threshold lemma: for a non-increasing sequence of non-negative integers satisfying a_{n+1} <= floor((1 - iota_tau) a_n), starting from a_0 = N, there exists finite n_0 <= N/iota_tau such that a_{n_0} = 0. Integer-valuedness forces exact termination.

registry_objects.title: Transporter-Hartogs Commutativity
registry_objects.summary: For any pair of sectors (X,Y), the transporter morphism Tr_{X->Y}: H_partial^(X) -> H_partial^(Y) commutes with Hartogs restriction maps. Transporters are morphisms of filtered modules over the holonomy grading.

registry_objects.title: Carriers as Germ Images
registry_objects.summary: Every carrier type (fiber, base, crossing) is a functorial image of the germ functor: Carrier_X = pr_X o Germ_omega. Carrier assignments are natural in the sector variable.

registry_objects.title: Single Scale Degree of Freedom
registry_objects.summary: tau-Schwarzschild has exactly one free scale parameter (linking mass M); all other quantities determined by M through iota_tau.

registry_objects.title: Minimal Mature Black Hole
registry_objects.summary: Minimal mass M_min exists for a dynamically stable black hole; below it, linking topology relaxes before torus vacuum stabilizes.

registry_objects.title: k* Selection Rule
registry_objects.summary: For each BH linking class l, there exists a canonical refinement depth k*(l) = min{n | N_n(x_l) subset N_BH}, the minimal depth at which the NF-prefix cylinder first fits inside the canonical BH neighborhood.

registry_objects.title: Clopen Nesting of NF-Prefix Cylinders
registry_objects.summary: Each NF-prefix cylinder N_n(x) is clopen in tau^3. The cylinders nest: N_{n+1}(x) subset N_n(x), with intersection_{n>=1} N_n(x) = {x}. Proved via fiber structure of NF map over discrete NFRep_k.

registry_objects.title: Idempotence of Norm_omega
registry_objects.summary: Norm_omega o Norm_omega = Norm_omega. At each stage n, NF_n maps into canonical representatives NFRep_n; applying NF_n to an element already in NFRep_n returns the same element.

registry_objects.title: Basin Preservation under Ringdown Dynamics
registry_objects.summary: If two BH states x, y share NF_n(x) = NF_n(y) at depth n, then after ringdown (post-merger relaxation) they satisfy NF_m(x) = NF_m(y) for all m >= n. Ringdown does not split dynamical basins.

registry_objects.title: Arrow of Time = Orbit Direction
registry_objects.summary: The temporal direction on tau^1 is the generative direction of the alpha-orbit (the direction in which rho acts): it is unique (exactly one direction of increasing n), irreversible (no operator maps alpha_{n+1} back to alpha_n), and structural (determined by the kernel axioms, not by thermodynamic arguments).

registry_objects.title: Pre-Temporal Indistinguishability
registry_objects.summary: In the pre-temporal epoch (n < n_ign): no physical subsystem can distinguish tick alpha_k from alpha_{k+1} by internal measurement, proper time t(n) exists mathematically but has no operational realization, and the causal ordering still holds but is not temporally articulated.

registry_objects.title: Mode Counting at Early Depths
registry_objects.summary: At the ignition depth n_ign, the spectral label set Lambda_{n_ign} contains all characters supported by the first n_ign primorial levels with mode count |Lambda| = prod_{k=1}^{n_ign} q_k. Every mode is active with nonzero amplitude -- no primorial filtering has yet occurred.

registry_objects.title: Null Character Uniqueness
registry_objects.summary: The null condition m^2(phi) = 0 uniquely selects the B-sector (EM) among the four matter sectors: D-sector (Gravity) has massive gravitons, A-sector (Weak) has massive W/Z bosons, C-sector (Strong) has confined gluons. Only the B-sector supports massless intertwiners.

registry_objects.title: CMB multipoles as boundary characters
registry_objects.summary: The CMB multipole coefficient a_{ell,m} is the (ell,m)-component of the boundary-character expansion of Sigma_CMB: a_{ell,m} = <chi_{ell,m}, Sigma_CMB>_{H_partial}, with the acoustic peaks controlled by kappa(omega)/kappa(B), damping tail by kappa(B;1), and ISW by kappa(D;1) = 1 - iota_tau.

registry_objects.title: Blackbody as coherence equilibrium
registry_objects.summary: A Planck blackbody spectrum is the unique energy distribution maximizing the refinement entropy S_ref at fixed total energy and photon number. The CMB's blackbody perfection reflects that Sigma_CMB is a coherence equilibrium state of the boundary holonomy algebra at n_rec.

registry_objects.title: CnuB mass constraint
registry_objects.summary: The CnuB echo surface constrains the total neutrino mass via the neutrino-to-matter density ratio: sum m_nu <= 0.12 eV (cosmological bound). The tau-prediction sum m_nu ~ 58 meV (from m_nu ~ m_e * iota_tau^15) is consistent with current bounds and testable by KATRIN and next-generation surveys.

registry_objects.title: Frame transitions are boundary-determined
registry_objects.summary: The frame adjacency map Phi_{k,k+1}^(n) between adjacent clopen frames at depth n is completely determined by the boundary holonomy algebra H_partial[omega] evaluated at the shared point alpha_{k+1}. No metric, connection, or gauge field data is needed.

registry_objects.title: BH gravitational Aharonov--Bohm phase
registry_objects.summary: The gravitational Aharonov-Bohm phase of a BH with mass M is Phi_BH = GM/iota_tau = (c^3/hbar)*iota_tau*M. The phase is proportional to both the mass and the master constant iota_tau -- a topological phase from circling a gravitational flux tube, yielding a measurable prediction.

registry_objects.title: Radiated energy bound
registry_objects.summary: The total energy radiated during a quasi-circular non-spinning BH merger satisfies Delta_E/((M_1+M_2)c^2) <= 1 - 1/sqrt(2) ~ 0.293. For equal-mass mergers, numerical relativity gives ~0.05, well below this bound. The maximum is achieved only in the extreme-spin Kerr limit.

registry_objects.title: Defect entropy converges to zero
